event: Value-read session shared to capture exact scanner sensor labels; monitor block read showing Fuel System, Catalyst and Oxygen Sensor Not completed
effect_on_data: Cancelled the planned Mode 06 read - nothing stored to read until a drive completes those monitors. Also produced docs/scanner-pids.md and the standing rule to request channels by their exact app label

event: Rule established: read the phone clock on every screenshot and never set a reading from one session against a reading from another
effect_on_data: Invalidated the assistant's attempt to use the 10:26-10:33 value reads to contradict the 12:48-12:51 graphs

event: Long term fuel trims read as learned for the first time after 3:06:10 of run time (+3.13 B1 / +2.34 B2)
effect_on_data: Removed the 'probably un-relearned' caveat that had qualified every earlier trim number, and killed the bank-asymmetry theory

event: Rule established: total fuel correction = short term + long term, so both halves of the same bank must be captured together
effect_on_data: Made every single-trim reading in the project uninterpretable on its own

event: The 2000 rpm load test run for the first time (idle to 2000 to idle) with STFT B1 paired against LTFT - B2
effect_on_data: Produced the load-cell finding: +2.34 at idle, 0 at 2000, returning instantly to exactly 2.34 - read as a fixed vacuum leak

event: The 2000 rpm test repeated with both banks' long term trim on one screen, held 2 min 7 s
effect_on_data: Confirmed both banks and revealed the correction is a gradient (idle +3.13/+2.34, just off idle +0.78, 2000 rpm 0) rather than a step

event: EVAP purge valve replaced with a new one
effect_on_data: The first repair in the owner's ownership to change the symptom - the shake disappeared in D and R and remained in P and N. Also invalidated every long term trim value learned around the old valve

event: Battery negative terminal disconnected and bridged to the positive post to drain capacitance - a full Keep Alive Memory wipe - performed at the same time as the purge valve change
effect_on_data: Erased learned long term trims (so the post-repair 0 percent readings are defaults, not learned zeros), the load-cell slope, the archived DTCs U0422 / U0140 / B11D8, the monitor results, freeze frame, and Mode 06. Short term trim survives because it does not depend on learning. Also created a two-variable confound with the valve replacement

event: Standing rule adopted: never wipe KAM before a measurement unless the wipe is the experiment
effect_on_data: Recorded in the repo to prevent a repeat

event: First Park versus Drive comparison of Engine RPM and Tim. adv. captured in one session, minutes apart
effect_on_data: Gave the first clean within-vehicle control: Park 44-55 rpm spans at a 3.4 s rhythm against Drive 13-18 rpm with no rhythm

event: Conclusion 'the hunt and the shake are one phenomenon' withdrawn after the owner said the shake moves him in the seat
effect_on_data: Reopened engine mounts (the D-versus-R argument only ruled out torque-reaction faults, not a mount that has lost its damping) and raised a contact point against the frame or cab as a new candidate

event: The relearning drive: 20-30 minutes mixed driving including steady cruise, deceleration fuel cut coasts on both banks, and wide open throttle pulls to 6832 rpm
effect_on_data: Relearned the adaptives, ran the catalyst and oxygen sensor monitors, and refilled Mode 06. Also produced the fuel cut and WOT eliminations

event: Rev limiter reached at 6832 rpm during the WOT pulls
effect_on_data: Offered as the likely explanation for the 2 and 1 raw misfire counts on cylinders 4 and 6 - the limiter cuts fuel and spark, which the misfire monitor can log

event: The neutral coast test withdrawn as unworkable on the owner's two objections
effect_on_data: Removed the only test designed to separate the vibration source from its transmission path; replaced with the stationary rpm sweep, the electrical load test and the touch test

event: RPM sweep in Park performed by feel (650 through 1800 rpm)
effect_on_data: Result 'worst idle at 650' argued against the half-order single-weak-cylinder signature and pointed at first order at 10.8 Hz sitting in the 8-15 Hz mount rock band. The follow-up clarification (sharp drop versus gradual taper) was never answered

event: Long term trims re-read at warm idle in Park with adaptives fully relearned: -0.78 both banks
effect_on_data: Closed the unmetered-air line - PCV, brake booster, manifold gasket, throttle body gasket, injector O-rings and the smoke test all withdrawn. The hunt was unchanged in the same capture, separating the leak from the hunt

event: Mode 06 on-board monitoring test results read for the first time on this truck
effect_on_data: Closed the ECU phase - per-cylinder misfire, both catalysts, all four O2 sensors, VVT and fuel system monitors all passed with margin. Killed the single-weak-cylinder hypothesis and the bank 1 downstream catalyst asymmetry

event: Fuel/Air com. ratio re-captured after the valve change and relearn, confirming the commanded square wave is unchanged (14.42 to 14.86 at about 3.5 s)
effect_on_data: Confirmed the PCM deliberately manipulates rpm, and that Mode 06's healthy sensors and catalysts make the slow 3.5 s period the expected behaviour rather than a fault

event: First phone accelerometer spectrum recorded with phyphox
effect_on_data: Unusable - axis spanned 0-210 Hz and the metadata (rpm, placement, engine state, noise floor) was not recorded. The measurement of the actual complaint remains outstanding

event: Prior history restated: an adaptive relearn plus 300 km had already been done before this repair and changed nothing
effect_on_data: Used as the argument that the KAM wipe alone cannot explain the D/R improvement, pointing at the valve instead

event: Evaporative System monitor still reads Not completed after the drive
effect_on_data: The only incomplete monitor; it checks the tank and canister for vapour leaks and sits behind a closed purge valve, so it cannot affect how the engine idles
